data.body:
Re-review after widening file_impact came back BLOCK, on a substantive finding I verified and accepted.

The gate found a SEVENTH consumer the plan never enumerated: llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py:108 short-circuits ("session_log", "code_review", "identity") to a bare exempt PASS, and imports nothing from rebar.types — grep confirms no EXEMPT reference in that module at all.

Verified, and the finding is right that it exists. But it is NOT another copy of this ticket set. PLAN_REVIEW_EXEMPT_TYPES is {bug, session_log, code_review, identity}; the short-circuit is that set MINUS bug, because since epic 6982/R4 a bug no longer short-circuits — it takes a light advisory review tier. The two answer different questions: is this type exempt from the CLAIM gate (this ticket), versus does this type skip review ENTIRELY (that one). Folding a set with different membership and different meaning into this consolidation would have CHANGED BEHAVIOUR rather than single-sourced anything — a bug would have started short-circuiting to a bare PASS, silently removing its review tier.

So the right resolution was not to widen the work but to make the claim accurate. The plan now names the seventh consumer explicitly and scopes it out with that reason, and the work is tracked as its own child, florid-cookable-fly (90cb-fe23-266e-41ac), linked discovered_from this ticket, with file_impact recorded and a derivation approach that keeps the two sets from drifting apart independently.

It is still a genuine mirror worth closing later: the three spellings must be TicketType members and nothing enforces it, so renaming code_review would silently switch its short-circuit off and it would start taking a full review with nothing failing — the same failure shape as every other finding in this epic.

Re-review started on the corrected plan.
